provenance: Telephone call, 2026-09-03, Larry's son asking the tier-1 questions from the interview guide and typing Larry's answers as he spoke them. The Camp Zama date question had been promoted to the head of the guide that morning. Raw capture: research/interviews/breakfast-questions.md, annotated in place under each question.
text: They were a free news paper, like 6 pages. I think the first page on the right side was 40 guys killed.
researchNotes: THIS REOPENS THE EDITION QUESTION AND CONTRADICTS THIS ARCHIVE'S CONCLUSION OF EARLIER THE SAME DAY. On the strength of a free stack at Camp Zama it had been reasoned that he read the Five-Star Edition, the Far East edition digitised in the NewspaperArchive holding being searched. But the Five-Star runs 24 to 37 pages and prints its casualty lists on inside pages - p32, p19, p13, p4 in the issues read. A SIX-PAGE free paper with a casualty item on page one, right-hand side, is not that publication. What he describes may be the Three-Star Edition, a hospital or post bulletin at Camp Zama, or a condensed edition; his page count may also be wrong sixty-one years on. Until this is settled, every negative recorded against the Five-Star Edition is against a paper he may never have read. See research/events/kia-misreport-stars-stripes.md.
